items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-08-01
items.q: That was my very dear friend. Joe thought it too well to me.

ctx.x: Oh, no. I didn't have to. Oh, no. He's quite a classical pianist. I don't think he swung like you did to tell you the truth. No, he didn't play like me. No. He didn't play like him. Joe Reitman. Mm-hmm. So you would naturally know him well.

That was my very dear friend. Joe thought it too well to me. He thought that it was just simply something that a man could sit on and know as many tunes as I knew without music. He couldn't get over that because that wasn't his category, don't you see? No. Now, this is my brother at the blue room when we were playing there.

items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-07-14
items.q: I have autographed pictures of Johnny Long, Joe Reichman, Paul Neighbors

ctx.x: I don't know. And the Blue Room, five years as an act, a jazz band, as long as five months at a time. And it broke all records for any bands being there. Because in those days, there were name bands that only came there and played one month at a time. Four weeks at a time. We were with, let me see, five months at one stretch, we were with five different bands. I have autographed pictures of Johnny Long, Joe Reichman, Paul Neighbors, all those bands, all those band leaders and everything in the different acts. But…
When you all played in the Blue Room, was that at the time when the Blue Room was broadcast on the radio?
